Bill.BriefDescription: Limiting mandatory overtime for corrections officers and sergeants employed by a county jail.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to limiting mandatory overtime for correctionsofficers and sergeants employed by a county jail; and adding a newsection to chapter 49.28 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 49.28 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The definitions in this subsection apply throughout thissection unless the context clearly requires otherwise. (a) "Employee" means a corrections officer or sergeant employed bya county jail located in a county with a population of more than onemillion five hundred thousand. (b) "Employer" means a county that is primarily responsible for theoperation of a jail. (c) "Jail" has the meaning provided in RCW 70.48.020. (d) "Overtime" means the hours worked in excess of an agreed upon,predetermined, regularly scheduled shift within a twentyfour hourperiod not to exceed eight and seventeen onehundredths hours in atwentyfour hour period or forty and eightyfive onehundredths hours p. 1 SSB 5907in a sevenday period, where the hours are worked in only five out ofthe seven days. (e) "Reasonable efforts" means that the employer, to the extentreasonably possible, does all of the following but is unable to obtainstaffing coverage: (i) Seeks individuals to volunteer to work extra time from allavailable qualified staff who are working; and (ii) Contacts qualified employees who have made themselvesavailable to work extra time. (f) "Unforeseeable emergent circumstance" means any unforeseen (i)declared national, state, or municipal emergency; or (ii) event thatposes a substantial risk for public safety or the safety of othercorrections officers. (2) Except as provided in subsection (3) of this section, anemployee may not be required to work more than four hours of overtimeper day. An employee may volunteer for additional overtime. Therefusal of an employee to volunteer for overtime work is not groundsfor discrimination, dismissal, discharge, or any other penalty, threatof reports for discipline, or employment decision adverse to theemployee. (3) An employee may be required to work more than four hours ofovertime per day if the employer has sought employee volunteers and hasnot had enough employees volunteer to meet sufficient staffing levelsand: (a) The work is due to an unforeseeable emergent circumstance; or (b) The employer documents that the employer has used reasonableefforts to obtain staffing. An employer has not used reasonableefforts to obtain staffing if overtime work is used to fill vacanciesresulting from chronic staff shortages.
